sections.h2: What Is an AI Video Ads Generator?
paras: It writes the script, picks a presenter, and lets you edit a short ad from the gray jar photo or the listing. The file is ready for a paid placement, and nobody has to film in the storeroom.

Publish it on [Instagram](page:plat-instagram), [Facebook](page:plat-facebook), or [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok). A feed post of the jar can be square at 1:1. A full-screen story wants 9:16. 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4 are available when the placement asks for them.

sections.h2: AI Video Ads From Your Jar
paras: Written From the Real Jar. If the jar is one ounce, the line can say one ounce.
Ready for a Paid Placement. A Reels placement wants the jar tall. A feed post can take the same jar as a square. Ask for 9:16 or 1:1, and use 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 when that placement asks.
More Than One Style. One cut can talk about how the cream feels on the skin. Another can open on the lid coming off. Keep the one that matches the jar you sell.

sections.h2: How to Make a Video Ad in 3 Simple Steps
paras: Upload Your Product Photo. Name the action first, such as a hand lifting the lid. Then paste the listing, or type one sentence about who the jar is for.
Share Your Video Idea. You get a clip back with someone speaking. The line can say how the cream sits on the skin, which is something you can show.
Download and Post. Save the file and put it in the ad account you already use for that jar. If the placement is a story, use the tall file. If it is a feed, use the square one.
Paste the listing in [URL to video](page:url-to-video), or choose the face in the [actor library](page:ai-actors). A second opening is another job from the same jar photo.

sections.h2: What Should the Clip Start With?
paras: Open with the jar already in a hand, as it comes out of the bag.
For this jar, show the lid twist or the jar lifted onto the counter. One action per clip. Ten seconds has room for that moment and a glimpse of the bathroom.
sections.alt: You open on the jar coming out of the tote: hands pull the gray skincare jar onto the bathroom counter.

sections.h2: How Long Should the Ad Be?
paras: Use 6 or 10 seconds for one action with the jar, 15 when the cream has to be used, and 30 for a fuller showing. Pick 9:16 so the clip fills the phone.

Six seconds is a lid coming off and costs 24 credits. Ten seconds fits that action plus a second look and costs 40. Fifteen can take the jar out, use it, and set it down, and costs 60. Thirty leaves room for a longer showing and costs 120. You see the number before you start.

Use 1:1 for a square scrolling post, 16:9 for a wide screen, and 3:4 or 4:3 when the placement asks for that shape. Each length or shape is a new clip. For a clip of the jar in use, start with [product videos](page:product-videos).
sections.alt: You can post the closing shot: hands shut the gray skincare jar on a neutral bedroom dresser.

paras: The file includes the spoken line, captions, and music you are allowed to run in an ad. Read the captions before you publish, and fix a wrong word before the ad goes live.

Put the words in the upper middle of a tall video, away from the app buttons at the bottom and the right edge. Use a face from the actor library and a logo you own. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded.

faq.q: What is an AI video ads generator, and what do I get for my shop?
faq.a: A tool that makes a short ad for a product you already sell. You bring the jar photo or the listing, and you get a file with someone speaking. This guide walks through each step.

faq.q: How do I create a video ad with AI?
faq.a: Start with the jar photo. Say the first action is the lid coming off. Download the tall file if the ad is a story, or the square file if it sits in the feed.

faq.q: Who is an AI video ad tool for?
faq.a: A shop that needs an ad for each product it sells this month. It is a poor fit when you only want one filmed founder story.

faq.q: Do I pay before the first ad?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. Each job shows its credit cost before it starts.

faq.q: Can I run the file as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. A paid plan includes commercial use, so you can put the file in an ad account, and the download has no watermark.

faq.q: Which shapes and platforms can I use?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for YouTube Shorts and TikTok, and 1:1 for a Facebook or Instagram feed. Use 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 when the placement names that shape.

faq.q: Can I make ads for many products?
faq.a: Yes. Run a batch across the products you choose. Each clip shows its credit cost before it starts. If a job fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Do these stand in for a creator?
faq.a: No. Use a generated clip when the jar needs three openings this week. Film the founder only when buyers expect that person on this one product.

faq.q: Will TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram reject the ad?
faq.a: These apps do not ban a generated ad as a category. They do care if the clip pretends a stranger bought the jar. Read that app's current ad rules before you spend, and read our [Content Policy](/content) for what you can upload.

faq.q: What if the clip shows a part my product does not have?
faq.a: Make the clip again and name the exact action and the exact jar in the sentence, so the lid and the shape match the photo.
